newsitem.title: UK: British firms infested by failed directors - study.
newsitem.headline: British firms infested by failed directors - study.

text.p: Nearly one in eight directors on the boards of British firms are "serial failures" who move from company to company leaving failed businesses in their wake, according to a study published on Monday.
The study, by information services company CCN Group, estimated that 307,000, or 11.9 percent, of British directors have multiple failed businesses in their past.
Of that number, some 4,000 have more than 10 failed companies to their discredit, the Nottingham-based group said.

"The activities of these people continue to present a huge risk to both businesses and individuals who deal with them," CCN said in its report, which called for stricter regulation of unlawful conduct and fraudulent trading.
Overall, almost one million directors -- 36.7 percent -- have been involved with at least one failed company, CCN said.
"Few lenders would regard association with just one failed company as a sign of dishonesty or incompetence," it said.
"The real problem is the "serial failure' who moves from one failed company to another, often deliberately closing down companies to avoid repaying their debts," the group added.
CCN said 45 percent of all "serial failures' live in London and southeast England, although the region is home to only 43 percent of all British directors.
The group compiled the study from a database including 2.6 million executive and non-executive directors registered with UK limited companies.
